summary: @servicetitan/quick-actions preinstall downloads Bun runtime and executes obfuscated sibling payload
details: Version 1.15.6 of @servicetitan/quick-actions declares a preinstall hook `node setup.mjs`. setup.mjs is itself obfuscated (hex-mangled identifiers, proxy-object string hiding) and, on install, downloads the Bun runtime from a GitHub releases zip into a temporary directory, extracts it, chmods it 0o755, then invokes `execFileSync(bun, ['math_init.js'])` against a bundled 727KB heavily obfuscated file (large numeric/string lookup array shuffled by `WV8StW`). The advertised purpose of the package is a React quick-actions UI library (peerDeps on mobx, react-dom, design-system); `math_init.js` has no relation to that purpose and is not referenced by any documented API — it is reached only by the install-time Bun invocation. The pattern is an alternate-runtime dropper: fetching a second language runtime at install time specifically to execute an opaque sibling blob evades Node-based scanners and delivers install-time code execution on any developer or CI host running `npm install`.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
